summary: The analysis reveals that clubs and doctors tables currently use text-based location fields (city, district, address) which lack referential integrity and data consistency. The locations table provides a hierarchical structure (counties → cities → sectors) with proper normalization. Recommendations include: (1) Add cityId, sectorId, and countyId foreign keys to clubs and doctors tables, (2) Keep address as text for street-level details, (3) Denormalize countyId for performance (enables county-level filtering without joins), (4) Maintain backward compatibility by keeping old columns temporarily, (5) Update all text-based indexes to foreign key indexes, (6) Add composite indexes for common query patterns (sportType + cityId, specialty + cityId). Users table currently has no location fields, but should optionally support cityId for parent location preferences. Migration requires fuzzy matching of existing text values to location IDs, with special handling for Bucharest sectors and Romanian diacritics variations.

phases.name: Schema Addition
phases.description: Add new foreign key columns alongside existing text columns. All new columns nullable initially to allow gradual data migration.

steps.sqlExample: ALTER TABLE clubs ADD COLUMN city_id TEXT REFERENCES locations(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT, ADD COLUMN sector_id TEXT REFERENCES locations(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT, ADD COLUMN county_id TEXT REFERENCES locations(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT;
steps.drizzleExample: cityId: text('city_id').references(() => locations.id, { onDelete: 'restrict' }), sectorId: text('sector_id').references(() => locations.id, { onDelete: 'restrict' }), countyId: text('county_id').references(() => locations.id, { onDelete: 'restrict' })

phases.name: Data Migration
phases.description: Populate new foreign key columns from existing text values using fuzzy matching and location lookup.

steps.description: Match existing city text values to locations table (type='city') using fuzzy matching for Romanian diacritics and variations
steps.sqlExample: UPDATE clubs SET city_id = (SELECT id FROM locations WHERE type = 'city' AND LOWER(UNACCENT(name)) = LOWER(UNACCENT(clubs.city)) LIMIT 1) WHERE city_id IS NULL;

steps.description: Match existing district text values to locations table (type='sector') for Bucharest clubs only
steps.sqlExample: UPDATE clubs SET sector_id = (SELECT id FROM locations WHERE type = 'sector' AND LOWER(UNACCENT(name)) = LOWER(UNACCENT(clubs.district)) AND parent_id IN (SELECT id FROM locations WHERE name = 'București' AND type = 'city') LIMIT 1) WHERE district IS NOT NULL AND city_id IN (SELECT id FROM locations WHERE name = 'București' AND type = 'city');
steps.drizzleExample: const sectorMatches = await db.select().from(locations).where(and(eq(locations.type, 'sector'), sql`LOWER(UNACCENT(${locations.name})) = LOWER(UNACCENT(${club.district}))`, inArray(locations.parentId, bucharestCityIds)));

steps.description: Derive countyId from cityId's parent relationship (cities belong to counties)
steps.sqlExample: UPDATE clubs SET county_id = (SELECT parent_id FROM locations WHERE id = clubs.city_id AND type = 'city') WHERE city_id IS NOT NULL AND county_id IS NULL;
steps.drizzleExample: const city = await db.query.locations.findFirst({ where: eq(locations.id, club.cityId) }); if (city?.parentId) { await db.update(clubs).set({ countyId: city.parentId }).where(eq(clubs.id, club.id)); }

steps.description: Match existing city text values to locations table (type='city') using fuzzy matching
steps.sqlExample: UPDATE doctors SET city_id = (SELECT id FROM locations WHERE type = 'city' AND LOWER(UNACCENT(name)) = LOWER(UNACCENT(doctors.city)) LIMIT 1) WHERE city_id IS NULL;

steps.description: Match existing district text values to locations table (type='sector') for Bucharest doctors only
steps.sqlExample: UPDATE doctors SET sector_id = (SELECT id FROM locations WHERE type = 'sector' AND LOWER(UNACCENT(name)) = LOWER(UNACCENT(doctors.district)) AND parent_id IN (SELECT id FROM locations WHERE name = 'București' AND type = 'city') LIMIT 1) WHERE district IS NOT NULL AND city_id IN (SELECT id FROM locations WHERE name = 'București' AND type = 'city');

steps.description: Derive countyId from cityId's parent relationship
steps.sqlExample: UPDATE doctors SET county_id = (SELECT parent_id FROM locations WHERE id = doctors.city_id AND type = 'city') WHERE city_id IS NOT NULL AND county_id IS NULL;

steps.sqlExample: SELECT id, name, city, district FROM clubs WHERE city_id IS NULL; SELECT id, first_name, last_name, city, district FROM doctors WHERE city_id IS NULL;

clubs.strategy: Fuzzy matching approach: (1) Normalize Romanian text (remove diacritics, lowercase) for comparison, (2) Exact match first (LOWER(UNACCENT(name)) = LOWER(UNACCENT(city))), (3) For Bucharest districts, match against sectors with parentId = Bucharest city ID, (4) Derive countyId from cityId's parent relationship, (5) Flag unmatched records for manual review. Handle special cases: 'București' vs 'Bucuresti', sector names like 'Sector 1' vs 'Sectorul 1'.
clubs.sqlExample: UPDATE clubs SET city_id = (SELECT id FROM locations WHERE type = 'city' AND LOWER(UNACCENT(name)) = LOWER(UNACCENT(clubs.city)) LIMIT 1), county_id = (SELECT parent_id FROM locations WHERE id = (SELECT id FROM locations WHERE type = 'city' AND LOWER(UNACCENT(name)) = LOWER(UNACCENT(clubs.city)) LIMIT 1)) WHERE city_id IS NULL;
challenges: City name variations (Cluj-Napoca vs Cluj Napoca)
Performance of fuzzy matching on large datasets

doctors.strategy: Same fuzzy matching approach as clubs: (1) Normalize Romanian text for comparison, (2) Exact match first, (3) For Bucharest districts, match against sectors, (4) Derive countyId from cityId, (5) Flag unmatched records. Doctors typically have fewer location variations than clubs.
doctors.sqlExample: UPDATE doctors SET city_id = (SELECT id FROM locations WHERE type = 'city' AND LOWER(UNACCENT(name)) = LOWER(UNACCENT(doctors.city)) LIMIT 1), county_id = (SELECT parent_id FROM locations WHERE id = (SELECT id FROM locations WHERE type = 'city' AND LOWER(UNACCENT(name)) = LOWER(UNACCENT(doctors.city)) LIMIT 1)) WHERE city_id IS NULL;
challenges: Smaller dataset than clubs (easier to handle)

users.strategy: No existing data to migrate - new columns are optional and will be populated as users update their profiles. No migration script needed.

backwardCompatibility.approach: Dual-write pattern: During transition period, write to both old text columns and new foreign key columns. Read from new columns, fallback to old columns if new columns are NULL. Deprecation markers in code comments. Gradual migration of read paths.
backwardCompatibility.duration: 3 months from Phase 5 completion. Allows time for: (1) All code paths to be updated, (2) Testing in production, (3) Monitoring for issues, (4) Manual review of unmatched locations.
backwardCompatibility.cleanupPlan: After 3 months: (1) Verify no code references old columns (grep search), (2) Remove deprecated columns from schema, (3) Drop text columns from database, (4) Update documentation. Keep migration scripts for historical reference.
